variants.title: A｜旧埠商港（1930年代意象）
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE full-width 16:9 landscape concept image for a first-person game set in an ORIGINAL FICTIONAL WUHAN on the Yangtze waterfront. This is one of three art-direction prototypes comparing eras. Render it like a compelling playable Fallen Aces-inspired environment: actual dimensional simple 3D architecture and props with rich selective hand-painted comic textures, strong dark structural ink strokes, deliberately blocked light/shadow, and ONE clearly 2D illustrated human sprite integrated into the scene. Crisp readable shapes, atmospheric distance, NO photographic realism, NO smooth generic AAA cinematic oil-paint concept art. It must feel like inhabitable comic space.
Shared composition for comparison: human eye height on the middle of broad worn embankment stone stairs, looking diagonally down and along the immense river, wide natural 70-degree field of view, no fisheye. The flood embankment and layered waterfront buildings fill the left third; stone stairs descend from the near left foreground to a landing at center; a low long working barge moored alongside the landing occupies the lower center-right; open Yangtze river fills the right half and recedes into distant opposite-bank lights. A single full-body 2D comic-drawn adult local courier stands on the landing near a bollard, in a muted red jacket appropriate to the era; black outlines and graphic shadow planes, feet grounded, natural scale, not a UI sticker. Thick mooring ropes, low gunwales, stairs, retaining wall and small warm shelters provide foreground/middle/background and playable spatial depth. The inland river is broad and turbid, low opposite bank, no sea cliffs or fantasy mountains. Wet evening just after rain with a little visible rain, indigo-blue-grey water, muted warm amber practical lamps, dark masonry, a controlled muted red accent. Maintain legibility in dark areas. Local Chinese waterfront life, Chinese signage only if natural, very few large readable characters such as "码头"; no English neon signs, no title cards or HUD or panel borders or comparison collages. A strong distinctive regional port-city identity rather than a generic alley. This is fictional urban design, not a reconstruction of any real historical building.

ERA A — a fictional 1930s-inspired Wuhan/Hankou river trading port, grounded noir adventure. Create soot-dark brick warehouses, deep shaded loading arches, weathered timber shopfronts, large Chinese brush-painted shipping signs, a small brick customs/port office with a squat clock or bell tower further up the left bank. Layered stone retaining walls, cargo hoists and simple derricks, sacks and timber crates as selective clusters, thick wood gangplank, timber-deck barge with a small soot-dark steam tug just beyond it. Oil lanterns and sparse early electric incandescent bulbs, cotton work jackets and worn leather satchel on the courier. The river horizon has steamship silhouettes and faint wharf lights, no modern skyscrapers, no modern suspension bridge, no plastic electronics. Convey commercial bustle that has quieted after rain, mysterious shadows and human warmth. Restrained ochre/ink-black under the shared blue-grey dusk. Invent original architecture, not Shanghai landmark replicas.

Large but distant practical port gantry cranes and one distant horizontal steel-truss river bridge fade into the mist. variants.title: B2｜旧工业江城＋轻蒸汽朋克
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / precise image edit.
Edit the supplied image, which is the BASE IMAGE, into a revised art-direction prototype B2 for an original alternate Wuhan Yangtze waterfront game. The user's request is: this circa-1990 industrial port feels not interesting enough; add a LITTLE steampunk to this version.

Preserve the fundamental identity: the same composition, human-eye view down the wet embankment steps, left-side Chinese worker canteen "职工食堂", brick workshops, broad river on the right, distant horizontal steel-truss bridge and port cranes, moored working barge, and the same red-jacketed 2D comic courier at the landing. Keep the grounded Chinese industrial working-port mood and warm inhabited pockets against cool rainy dusk. Preserve the graphic hand-inked comic treatment, dimensional architecture, clear blocked shadows, and flat illustrated human appearance. This remains an old Wuhan-inspired working waterfront, with selectively retrofitted steam technology. Roughly eighty percent familiar port, twenty percent playful mechanical invention.

Make THREE specific, visually legible improvements, with a few memorable large shapes rather than a blanket of tiny gears:
1. The foreground barge becomes a locally improvised steam-assisted utility barge. Keep its hull and boxy warm-lit cabin, but install one compact, clearly visible weathered cylindrical boiler with a ribbed heat shield, a large round pressure gauge, a single exposed piston/flywheel assembly and short flanged pipes on the near deck. Dark enamel green, blackened iron, small patches of aged copper, and one red handwheel. The equipment must feel operable and sized for this actual small working boat, not a giant ornate ship. A controlled curl of pale steam catches the warm cabin light.
2. Beside the canteen doorway, add a modest riveted steam food cabinet / noodle steamer, linked to a visible practical wall steam pipe with an elbow and valve. A cook-visible warm interior and escaping soft steam blend food warmth with the industrial system. Keep the sign, small dining room, bicycle and local street-life details recognizable. No Victorian saloon, no top hats or fantasy costumes.
3. At the warehouse landing behind and slightly above the courier, add one distinctive small steam-powered cargo hoist: a curved iron support arm, chunky mechanical winch, round gauge, and a suspended rectangular cargo cradle holding a couple of sacks. A short service platform and ladder connect it to the workshop. Its silhouette should make a viewer curious about the space without swallowing the skyline or blocking the walkable landing.

Make the added steam, valves, circular gauge and curved hoist shape easy to notice in a full-frame view. Let the courier carry a small practical canvas tool satchel while retaining the same character and red work jacket. The river remains a large calm breathing space; keep the stairs-to-landing-to-barge route open and visually inviting. Preserve enough shadow structure, but lift local midtones on the new mechanisms so their function reads. Maintain warm amber / cold blue-grey with muted oxidized-green and copper accents. Do not make the whole image sepia or brass. No cyberpunk neon, no airships, no fantasy skyline, no decorative gear wallpaper, no huge weapon, no HUD, no title text, no collage.
Output ONE full-frame landscape image with the same aspect ratio and scene as the supplied reference.
